description: Interfaz para la prevención de problemas psicomotores para astronautas en misiones en diferentes niveles de gravedad.
summary:
We developed AURA (Astronaut Unified Readiness and Autonomous Health), an integrated personalized medicine ecosystem designed to safeguard astronaut health during deep-space missions. The system combines three components: AURA Manager, a mission-control web platform that cross-references flight schedules with biometric telemetry and an adaptive 5-question daily check-in; minimalist mixed-reality glasses displaying real-time workout guidance, crew status, and instant visual alerts; and a full-body biometric suit equipped with lower-limb surface electromyography (sEMG), heart rate, and SpO2 sensors.

Prolonged microgravity induces severe muscle atrophy, bone demineralization, orthostatic intolerance, and balance loss. AURA addresses this challenge by detecting early neuromuscular and physiological decline—filtering out symptom underreporting—and dynamically tailoring daily exercise, nutrition, and supplementation protocols to each astronaut's needs before gravity transitions occur.

This capability is critical for upcoming lunar and Martian exploration. Unlike Earth returns, where medical teams assist astronauts immediately after splashdown, crew members landing on Mars (0.38g) will have zero external support. AURA ensures astronauts arrive strong and ready to exit the spacecraft and take their first steps on any planet on their own two feet.
details:
AURA (Astronaut Unified Readiness & Autonomous-health) helps astronauts keep the physical capacities they need for every day of a mission: strength, balance, coordination and exercise tolerance. Above all, it helps them arrive at each gravity change (landing, leaving the spacecraft, returning to Earth) able to walk out on their own feet.

WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS

AURA has two connected parts:

- AURA Manager is a web console for mission control. It defines the mission timeline and a prevention plan: exercise, assessments, supplements, recovery, and preparation for gravity transitions. It publishes all of this as a versioned, checksummed "mission package". It also reviews every change the astronaut's interface makes and receives its alerts.

- AURA Astronaut is the astronaut's interface, designed for mixed-reality glasses: mission information floats over the astronaut's real view of the cabin, so they never have to stop and pick up a device. For the hackathon we built it as an Android app running on a tablet that stands in for the glasses. The rear camera shows the surroundings and the HUD is drawn on top, just as it would appear in a passthrough headset. It behaves as an on-board agent. It loads the mission package, follows Mission Elapsed Time (MET) and flight days, shows today's plan and the next recommended action, and gives a countdown to the next gravity transition. It collects the astronaut's data: activity confirmations, a short daily questionnaire whose questions change with the mission phase, and live heart rate from a standard Bluetooth LE watch. Smart-clothing signals and the coordination test are simulated for now and always labelled as simulated.

With that data it shows a traffic light for each capacity: green, amber, red, or gray when there is not enough data. The color never appears alone: it always comes with a reason, the value and the threshold. When the indicators deviate, the app adapts the plan on its own, only within the limits mission control allows. It can swap an exercise for a lighter one, move it, or skip it, always with a reason, and it never increases the load or touches fixed operations. Each adaptation is applied on board immediately and sent to mission control for validation without blocking the crew. What adapting cannot fix (a capacity in red, a lost transition-preparation measure, self-reports that contradict sensor data) is sent as an alert. Important messages are also spoken aloud through offline text-to-speech.

As a gravity change approaches, a dedicated panel gathers what matters for egress. It shows the trend of critical capacities against the astronaut's own baseline: orthostatic tolerance and balance on a short flight like Artemis II. It also shows whether preparation measures were completed: aerobic exercise, fluid loading, compression garment and return preparation.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

- More crew autonomy: decisions happen on board and offline, which matters more as communication delays grow on the way to the Moon and Mars.

- Mission control keeps authority: it decides what can be adapted, and sees and validates every change.

- AURA protects today without sacrificing tomorrow. Removing a workout protects the astronaut today, but each missed session costs preparation, so AURA tracks what was planned against what was done and flags any lost preparation.

- It is mission-agnostic. Artemis II is our validation case, built on NASA's planned Artemis II timeline, but everything mission-specific comes in the package, so the same app can serve lunar, Mars or space-station missions.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES

- Android app: Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, CameraX, Room, kotlinx.serialization, Android TextToSpeech and the Bluetooth LE API (heart rate via the standard 0x180D profile, tested with a Garmin Forerunner 745). Tested on a Xiaomi Pad 5 tablet.

- Mission control console: TypeScript, Next.js and React, deployed on Vercel.

- A shared JSON contract between the two parts, and unit tests for package parsing and adaptation rules.

- Anatomy: a 3D human silhouette derived from BodyParts3D (DBCLS, CC BY-SA).

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

- AURA is meant to be worn: a mixed-reality HUD that keeps the astronaut's hands and attention free for the task. A rotating holographic body shows which muscle groups are working, using motion sensors as a stand-in for smart clothing. A heart in its chest beats at the astronaut's real heart rate and sends out a ring of light, the "aura", on every beat.

- The daily questionnaire is adaptive: it picks its questions from the mission context, such as an upcoming transition, a recent spacewalk or days spent in microgravity.

- AURA treats the gravity transition as the goal the whole mission prepares for.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

- Safety and ethics: AURA does not diagnose and never certifies anyone as "fit". All thresholds are demonstration values and labelled as such. Simulated data is always marked on screen and in storage.

- Privacy: health data stays on the device. Only adaptations and alerts, with their evidence, are sent.

- Operations: it works fully offline and in airplane mode. The HUD is designed for one hand and gloves, with high contrast over any background. The voice never repeats itself and can be muted.

- Inclusiveness: the interface is fully bilingual (English and Spanish), as are the mission package texts.
